text:
Stretched out,

stone made of midday,

half-closed eyes where white shades into blue,

a half-open smile.

You rise halfway and shake your lion’s mane.

Then you lie down,

a slender groove of lava in the rock,

a sleeping bolt.

While you sleep I caress and polish you,

slender axe,

arrow with which I set the night on fire.


Far off the sea battles with swords and feathers.

translation.title: Lightning at Rest
translation.editorial_note: The reclining beloved remains stone, lava, lightning, axe, and arrow in one continuous sculptural sequence; the distant sea answers with its own weapons and softness.
